calibration.nextAction: OBTAIN_CODEX_SIGHTED_ACCEPTANCE, and rule on the single-arm verdict question above. The computed half for mate and sobrio is done and receipted on three verticals through both doors; SIGHTED_ACCEPTED is not claimable from a computed run.
calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: Decoration intensity is ADDITIVE over a hierarchy it must not author. So the negative set is the whole non-decoration surface of the measured root: its box (control height remains fixed, bound to card-modern-md/root and carrying the two @rect-* observables so a transform or zoom cannot hide behind an unmoved longhand), its type, its base fill and border COLOR, its border widths and radii, and its motion. What is deliberately NOT in the set is the pair the control owns and must move: box-shadow's inset optical keyline and background-image's surface tint. 'touch target remains fixed' is deliberately NOT declared: it is a declared-targets phrase and the only bindable target here is a Card root, which is not a control-bearing element. Declaring it and binding it to a non-control would report a real assertion about a target it was never about; declaring it and leaving it unbound would fail the run closed. The box-geometry claim it would have made on this root is already made by 'control height remains fixed', whose property set covers both axes through @rect-inline-size/@rect-block-size.
calibration.evidenceKindLabellingRule: Every one of the six artifacts proves BOTH a computed delta and an exact restore; each is a three-phase both-arm run. evidenceKind names the ROLE the receipt is claimed for, not the only thing its artifact contains: the three mate receipts are claimed as static-db-computed-parity and the three sobrio receipts as exact-restore. A reader who wants the other half of either receipt will find it in the same artifact.

measuredResult.scenarios: 6 = {rottay,bithire,evnto} x {mate,sobrio}, both ingress doors on ONE scene, both themes. All six self-check harness-live; ingressEquivalence identical with 0 differing rows in all six; restore.exact true and negativeControls.held true on every arm of every scenario.
measuredResult.directChannel: --ds-effect-intensity read directly on token-readout moved on BOTH arms in all six scenarios: rottay/evnto 1 -> 0 and 1 -> 0.6; bithire 0.58 -> 0 and 0.58 -> 0.6. The bithire baseline is 0.58 because its compiled artifact authors that floor, which is also the precedent the estandar law cites.
measuredResult.paintedDelta: card-modern-md/root background-image, first gradient stop alpha: 0.024 -> 0 at mate and 0.024 -> 0.016 at sobrio, in rottay and evnto, on both arms and both themes. Monotonic (0 < 0.016 < 0.024). The authored ramp is 0.025 * effectIntensity; Chromium serialises rgba alpha at 8-bit precision, so 0.025 reads 0.024 and 0.015 reads 0.016. The quantisation is the browser's, not a compiler rounding, and it is recorded rather than smoothed away.
measuredResult.armEquivalence: 0 differing rows between static-brand-theme and db-tenant-theme in all six scenarios. Static and DB equivalence is a measured diff on one DOM here, not an inference from two separate runs.

knownDefects.finding: The elevated card's intensity-scaled optical keyline does not respond to the dial. card.css declares `box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 color-mix(in srgb, var(--ds-color-bg-elevated) calc(72% * var(--ds-effect-intensity)), transparent), var(--ds-card-elevated-shadow, var(--ds-card-shadow))` and its own comment says the keyline dissolves at intensity 0. MEASURED: box-shadow is byte-identical across baseline and mutation in all 24 arm-rows of all six scenarios, in both themes, on both doors.
knownDefects.scope: This is a measured non-response, NOT a diagnosis. This packet did not determine WHY -- whether another declaration wins the cascade for this element, or the composed term resolves to a value indistinguishable from the one it replaces. Owner ruling for this packet was explicitly to record it and not chase it, because background-image is an independent painted witness of the same channel and already carries the canary.
knownDefects.whyItIsNotAFalseNegativeForThisControl: The control is proven live on this exact element by a DIFFERENT painted property (background-image) on the same root in the same runs, and proven live at the channel by the direct read. So 'the dial is inert' is refuted independently of the keyline.

knownDefects.finding: In bithire the dial reaches the channel but paints NOTHING on the card. The channel moves 0.58 -> 0 / 0.6 on both doors, and card-modern-md/root shows 0 moved properties. Cause is source-visible: bithire's compiled artifact flat-declares --ds-gradient-surface as an opaque three-stop literal (linear-gradient(145deg, #FFFFFF 0%, #F7FAFC 58%, #F5F2EC 100%)) carrying no intensity term, so the card's surface tint cannot scale there, while rottay and evnto inherit the intensity-scaled definition from foundation/animations/premium.css.
knownDefects.boundedBy: It is a per-tenant authoring divergence, not a broken lowering: both doors agree with each other in bithire too (0 differing rows), and the same stop paints in the other two verticals through the same code.

openContractQuestions.question: estandar (1) has no receipted computed run, and the reason is an instrument limitation rather than a missing measurement. The stop is reachable only through the static door by contract, so it must be run single-arm; but a single-arm causal run reports ingressEquivalenceHeld=false (comparable=false is folded into 'did not hold'), which forces verdict.pass=false and exitCode 1, and the receipt validator refuses a non-zero exit for any evidenceKind except negative-drill. Forcing both arms is impossible: the DB arm throws at lowering, which is the very behaviour under test.
openContractQuestions.whatWasMeasuredAnyway: A single-arm static run on bithire WAS harness-live: --ds-effect-intensity moved 0.58 -> 1 on both themes, negative controls held, restore exact. rottay and evnto were correctly refused as harness-suspect for a different and honest reason -- their compiled baseline is ALREADY 1, so estandar is a no-op there and no movement exists to observe.
openContractQuestions.reproduce: node src/tooling/resolution-probe/public/cli/index.mjs causal --control-manifest manifest/controls/surfaces.effect-intensity.json --family-manifest manifest/families/primitive/display/card.json --stop estandar --vertical bithire --arm static-brand-theme --fixture card-modern-md --fixture token-readout --bind control-height-fixed=card-modern-md/root
openContractQuestions.proposedResolution: DT ruling needed on whether a deliberately single-arm causal run may report ingressEquivalence as NOT-COMPARABLE without failing its verdict. Reporting 'the two doors disagreed' when only one door was measured is the same class of error the measurement guards exist to refuse. This packet did NOT change that semantics: weakening a verdict rule is an owner decision, not a lane decision.

dischargedContractQuestions.question: Prove the two doors agree for the stops that are inside the tenant envelope, and prove the envelope REJECTS rather than clamps outside it.
dischargedContractQuestions.outcome: Discharged in both halves. Agreement is a measured 0-differing-row diff on one DOM for mate and sobrio in all three verticals. Rejection is proven against the productive DB door for estandar (1) in all three verticals with code invalid_value at $.appearance.surfaces.effectIntensity, and the ceiling value itself (0.65/0.65/0.75) is separately shown to be ACCEPTED in the same test, which is what separates a rejection from a clamp.
dischargedContractQuestions.evidence: packages/core/src/infrastructure/compilers/composition/tenant-theme/tests/surfaces-effect-intensity-envelope.test.ts (20 assertions, all green) plus the six causal receipts.

dischargedContractQuestions.question: Prove the envelope is a closed interval, not a one-sided ceiling.
dischargedContractQuestions.outcome: Discharged. A value below the floor (-0.1) and a value above the global cap (1.5) are both refused on the DB door in all three verticals, with the same invalid_value code and path as the ceiling case.

dischargedContractQuestions.question: Does the harness lower a BOUNDED control correctly? spacing.rhythm is closed-enum, where the stop id IS the value a tenant writes, so nothing had ever exercised the other shape.
dischargedContractQuestions.outcome: Discharged, and discharging it required an instrument fix: it did NOT. buildIngressInput wrote the stop ID at the ingress path for every domain kind, so this control would have lowered --ds-effect-intensity: mate. The static lowering is String(su.effectIntensity ?? 1) with no numeric guard, so the NAME reached the channel verbatim; --ds-effect-intensity is a registered @property with syntax '<number>' and initial-value 1, so the declaration is invalid at computed-value time and the browser substitutes 1. Every stop would have painted the baseline and the run would have reported a LIVE control as inert, while the arm still carried a non-empty variable map so no existing guard would have fired. The harness now derives the written value from domain.kind and fails closed on any kind it cannot write.
dischargedContractQuestions.evidence: packages/core/src/tooling/resolution-probe/runtime/ingress/tests/index.test.mjs -- 31 assertions green, including a counterfactual that drives the REAL compiled compileBrandTheme with the stop NAME and pins that it emits the literal 'mate', plus fail-closed drills for a bounded stop with no finite value and for every domain kind the harness cannot write.

unmeasuredScope: Responsive divergence. The probe pins one viewport (1280x800, dpr 1), so no claim is made about this control at another breakpoint. Recorded as honest debt, not as a passing row.
